title: Hyperparameter Scaling Laws Across MoE Sparsity
abstract: arXiv:2609.08690v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models expand model capacity without a proportional increase in training compute, but increasing sparsity makes reliable hyperparameter transfer challenging. In this work, we show that conventional hyperparameter scaling laws are insufficient for ultra-sparse MoEs: the optimal learning rate and batch size vary with activation ratio, and these shifts cannot be explained by either total or activated parameter count alone. To characterize this dependence, we conduct 1,800 pre-training runs spanning six activated-parameter scales and models with up to 6B total non-embedding parameters, processing approximately 20 trillion tokens at a cost of 200,000 equivalent H800 GPU-hours. Our results reconcile conflicting findings in prior work by revealing two scaling regimes. translated_title: 跨MoE稀疏度的超参数缩放定律
translated_abstract: 混合专家模型能够在训练计算量不成比例增加的情况下扩展模型容量，但随着稀疏度的提高，可靠地迁移超参数变得具有挑战性。在本工作中，我们证明传统的超参数缩放定律对于超稀疏MoE模型是不够的：最优学习率和批量大小会随激活比率而变化，且这些变化无法仅用总参数量或激活参数量来解释。为了刻画这种依赖关系，我们进行了1,800次预训练实验，涵盖六个激活参数规模、总非嵌入参数量高达6B的模型，处理了约20万亿个token，成本相当于200,000个H800 GPU小时。我们的结果通过揭示两种缩放机制，调和了先前工作中相互矛盾的发现。在固定稀疏度下，最优批量大小与训练token数 $D$ 呈幂律关系，而最优学习率随训练…
tldr: 本研究通过1,800次预训练实验（约20万亿token）发现MoE模型的最优学习率和批量大小随激活比率而非参数量变化，并揭示了两种缩放机制，从而调和了以往研究中相互矛盾的发现。
en_tdlr: By conducting 1,800 pre-training runs totaling ~20 trillion tokens, this study shows that the optimal learning rate and batch size of MoE models shift with the activation ratio rather than parameter count, and identifies two scaling regimes that reconcile conflicting findings in prior work.
